preconditions.description: The input contains at least two lines: the first with n and the second with the sequence of group sizes.
The number of groups n is an integer between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: groups := list(map(int, lines[1].split())); len(groups) == n and all(x in (1, 2) for x in groups)
preconditions.description: The second line contains exactly n integers, each being either 1 or 2.

postconditions.expression: count1 := sum(1 for x in groups if x == 1); count2 := sum(1 for x in groups if x == 2); total_people = count1 + 2 * count2; max_teams = min(count2, count1) + (total_people - 3 * min(count2, count1)) // 3 if count1 >= count2 else (count1 // 3) + count2; output == str(max_teams)
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum number of teams of three. This is calculated by first pairing as many groups of 2 with groups of 1 as possible (since a group of 2 must stay together and needs exactly one person of 1 to form a team of 3), and then forming teams from the remaining groups of 1 (three 1s make a team). If there are more groups of 2 than 1, the excess groups of 2 cannot form teams because they cannot be split and no 1s remain to complete them.
